title: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
description: Master the Critical View of Safety (CVS) and avoid vascular/biliary injuries.

start.text: Ports are placed. The fundus is retracted cephalad, and the infundibulum is retracted laterally. You are exposing Calot's triangle.

dissection_start.text: What is your first major dissection step?

options.label: Incise the peritoneum over the hepatocystic triangle
Clip the largest tubular structure visible
options.feedback: Catastrophic error. You clipped the Common Bile Duct (CBD) because you did not achieve the Critical View of Safety.

clear_fat.text: You are clearing the hepatocystic triangle of fibrofatty tissue. You see two tubular structures entering the gallbladder. What is the next mandatory step for the Critical View of Safety (CVS)?

options.label: Clip and divide both structures immediately
options.feedback: You have not met all 3 criteria for CVS. You must clear the cystic plate.

options.label: Separate the lower third of the gallbladder off the cystic plate (liver bed)

cvs_achieved.text: CVS Achieved: 1) Hepatocystic triangle cleared, 2) Lower third separated from liver bed, 3) Only two structures enter the gallbladder.

fail_cbd_injury.text: Procedure Failed: Common Bile Duct Injury.

fail_no_cvs.text: Procedure Failed: Premature clipping without CVS.

success.text: Procedure Successful: Safe dissection and clipping.
